scientific_question: Can raw typed relations support one full-pool selector without losing routing inputs?
architecture: Keep native routing paths; shared 128d four-layer relation-aware node core; original two-layer node-solver dual stream and utility head; per-edge bias plus message
supervision: Native routing CE; best-set CE for new integer tasks; full-information soft risk; optional advantage head for D1
matched_comparison: Same architecture in both D1 and D2 arms; do not attribute their contrast to the frontend
meaningful_support: Natural-domain hard choices improve with preserved task and candidate identities
falsifier: Only task-size priors or TRAIN fit improve; structure-dependent errors remain
not_novel_by_itself: Calling a graph transformer universal or adding a type token without preserving edges
main_limits: Input sufficiency is not finite-depth expressivity; memory feasibility remains unmeasured

scientific_question: Does explicit structure-family supervision improve transferable full-candidate advantage learning beyond the same endpoint labels?
architecture: A1 with one shared candidate representation feeding utility and centered advantage prediction
supervision: Signed native centered advantages on fixed TRAIN scales; endpoint anchors; true-family response differences; natural selection loss
matched_comparison: Same endpoint tables and exposure: static endpoints versus true-family response; shuffled-pair variant must recompute correct targets
meaningful_support: Cross-base response beats zero and TRAIN-mean baselines and improves natural hard choices with no offsetting damage
falsifier: Base memorization; generated-domain-only gains; lower response error without selection gains
not_novel_by_itself: R114 already had full-pool labels; R115 already used centered multivariate responses; a neural replacement alone is not new
main_limits: Family support shift; correlated endpoints; stochastic solver realizations; cost of full declared pool per endpoint

scientific_question: Does whole-model hard-action constraint feedback improve the objective actually deployed?
architecture: Same A1 and single-checkpoint argmax; no query probes or bias-only rescue
supervision: Native versus best-set hard error; routing actual relative regret; nonrouting zero-safe scaled absolute loss; frozen fixed36 target
matched_comparison: Same natural full information and initialization source: fixed composite proxies versus hard TRAIN violation feedback
meaningful_support: Lower hard error with protected routing and nonrouting risks and genuine rescued opportunities
falsifier: Only soft probabilities or selection counts improve; hard tradeoffs persist; TRAIN feasibility does not generalize
not_novel_by_itself: Adding regret loss alone repeats earlier project work
main_limits: Proxy looseness; nonconvex optimization; one checkpoint has no stochastic-mixture feasibility guarantee

scientific_question: If dense attention is the bottleneck can global communication be made cheaper without dropping raw relations?
architecture: True-edge messages plus inducing global tokens plus candidate access to all nodes
supervision: Same selection and advantage semantics as A1
matched_comparison: Do not add simultaneously to initial D1 or D2 comparison; later compare same raw inputs
meaningful_support: Reduced global-attention burden without hard-choice degradation
falsifier: Latent compression loses long-range or combinatorial advantage information
not_novel_by_itself: A latent interface or more pooling is not a new scientific mechanism
main_limits: Dense raw E remains quadratic; fixed inducing count may bottleneck information

scientific_question: If observed early cross-domain interference persists would small family adapters help?
architecture: Shared main core with small relation-family adapters rather than 24 independent networks
supervision: Same task-equal objective; no forced per-deployment frequency
matched_comparison: Only after isolating structure-dependent interference; retain comparable capacity and input semantics
meaningful_support: Matched natural-domain gains beyond shared A1
falsifier: Only parameter count or TRAIN fit improves; routing degrades
not_novel_by_itself: Late private candidate branches and generic modules were already explored
main_limits: Fragmented data and weak family transfer; no claim of inevitable negative transfer

scientific_question: Would meta-gradient weighting add information beyond hard-risk feedback?
supervision: Any future meta subset must remain inside TRAIN; formal VAL only for selection
matched_comparison: Not part of initial one or two bounded comparisons
meaningful_support: A future independent comparison would need hard-decision rather than weighted-loss gains
falsifier: Extra weighting only optimizes surrogate or leaks formal VAL into update gradients
not_novel_by_itself: Meta reweighting is an existing mechanism not a substitute for D2
main_limits: Higher-order overhead and different validation semantics
